NAME: PersistentPhysicalTiltProfitErosion
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(TREND(RATIO(capx, ADD(capx, COALESCE(xrd, 0))), 3)), RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), at), 3))))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms persistently shifting investment toward physical capex while gross-profit productivity trends down should earn lower future returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: This focuses on sustained reallocation of investment capacity, rather than a one-period capex spike. A persistent physical tilt is most concerning when the firm’s operating franchise is deteriorating, suggesting tangible expansion is not being supported by productive intangible capability.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(VOL(RATIO(capx, at), 5)), SUB(RANK(VOL(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 5)), RANK(TREND(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5))))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms with volatile capex and volatile R&D intensity but no improving margin trend should earn lower future returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The mechanism is unstable coordination between tangible and intangible investment programs. R&D volatility can be constructive if it produces margin improvement, but when paired with lumpy physical investment and weak margin trends it may indicate unfocused capital allocation.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

NAME: CapacityInventoryNoInnovation

HYPOTHESIS: Gross physical capacity expansion should predict lower returns when inventories build faster than R&D intensity improves.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Expanding gross PPE is most problematic when it is accompanied by poor sell-through rather than renewed innovation effort. The balanced spread distinguishes capacity additions tied to inventory accumulation from capacity additions supported by rising knowledge investment.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

NAME: RDGrossProfitSellThrough
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(DELTA(MA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 3), 1)), SUB(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), at), 1)), RANK(DELTA(RATIO(invt, sale), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Rising R&D intensity should predict higher returns when it is validated by improving gross-profit productivity rather than inventory buildup.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This refines R&D commercialization by focusing on gross-profit validation instead of raw sales growth. High scores identify firms increasing knowledge investment while operating output improves and working-capital overhang does not rise.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: GoodwillDrawdownNoReinvestment
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at), 1))), SUB(RANK(NEG(DELTA(MA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 3), 1))), RANK(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, ppent), 5))))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms with goodwill drawdowns and weakening R&D intensity, without offsetting physical refresh investment, should earn lower future returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: A goodwill decline can reflect impairment or deterioration in acquired intangible value. It is most concerning when the firm is also cutting organic knowledge investment and not refreshing its tangible base, suggesting acquired assets are decaying without replacement.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: EquityFinanceInnovationValidated
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(sstk, at)), SUB(SUMRANK(DELTA(MA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 3), 1), DELTA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), at), 1)), SUMRANK(DELTA(RATIO(capx, at), 1), DELTA(RATIO(invt, sale), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Equity issuance should have better return implications when it funds rising R&D intensity and gross-profit improvement rather than capex and inventory buildup.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Equity financing is more appropriate for risky intangible investment than for conventional empire-building. The balanced use-of-proceeds spread rewards issuers with innovation and operating validation, while penalizing issuers whose financing coincides with tangible expansion and working-capital accumulation.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

RATIONALE: This is a horizon-lengthened clone of the archived PhysicalTiltGrossProfitMiss (same two legs, TREND(3) substituted for DELTA(1)), a cosmetic variant of an already-strong signal rather than a new mechanism.

---CRITIQUE UnstableDualInvestmentNoMarginTrend---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: Sits squarely on top of the archived MoatFragileCapexLumpiness (same capex-volatility gate with a reshuffled second leg), and the R&D-intensity volatility term is degenerate for the large mass of COALESCE-to-zero non-R&D firms, so the "instability" leg largely proxies for R&D reporting status.

---CRITIQUE CapacityInventoryNoInnovation---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: A coherent and genuinely new pairing — gross-capacity expansion gated on inventory build versus R&D improvement — that is a recombination of archived ingredients but not a duplicate of any single prior signal (CapacityBuildDemandOptionGap used sales productivity, not inventory), with sign and expression consistent.

---CRITIQUE RDGrossProfitSellThrough---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: Identical in structure and hypothesis to the archived RDSpendSellThroughValidation with only GROWTH(sale) swapped for DELTA(gross profit/at); the swap is not motivated by any diagnosis of that signal's fmb/alpha disagreement and reads as a one-term cosmetic edit.

---CRITIQUE GoodwillDrawdownNoReinvestment---

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: ProcessRDCapexCostRelief
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(capx, ppent), 1)), SUB(RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(cogs, sale), 1))), RANK(NEG(DELTA(MA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 3), 1)))))
HYPOTHESIS: Capex refresh should predict higher returns when it is associated with falling cost intensity and no cutback in R&D intensity.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: This moves away from the physical-share-versus-profit-erosion clone and instead tests whether tangible refresh is part of process innovation. The signal rewards capex only when costs improve and R&D is maintained or rising, distinguishing productive modernization from simple physical expansion.

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: InvestmentMixInstabilityNoMoat
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(VOL(RATIO(capx, ADD(capx, COALESCE(xrd, 0))), 5)), RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5))))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms with unstable allocation between capex and R&D while gross margins trend down should earn lower future returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: This replaces separate capex-volatility and R&D-volatility legs with volatility of the tangible-versus-R&D investment mix itself. For non-R&D firms the share is stable rather than mechanically volatile, so the signal focuses on allocation instability rather than R&D reporting status.

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: RDPerEmployeeAssetLightScale
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), emp), 1)), SUB(RANK(GROWTH(sale, 1)), RANK(GROWTH(ppent, 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms increasing R&D per employee while scaling sales faster than physical assets should earn higher future returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: This is not another R&D sell-through versus inventory variant; it tests whether knowledge intensity per worker is translating into asset-light commercial scale. The physical-investment comparison enters through PP&E growth, so the signal distinguishes scalable intangible productivity from growth requiring heavy tangible expansion.

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: GoodwillCapexSupportBurden
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), ADD(ppent, COALESCE(gdwl, 0)))), SUB(RANK(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, ppent), 5)), RANK(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Goodwill-heavy firms requiring unusually high capex support without margin improvement should earn lower future returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: This avoids the goodwill-drawdown gate and instead uses goodwill concentration as an acquired-intangible overhang measure. High capex intensity is penalized only when it appears necessary to support goodwill-heavy assets without improving margins.

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: KnowledgeOperatingLeverage
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(SUB(RANK(GROWTH(sale, 1)), RANK(GROWTH(emp, 1)))), SUB(RANK(MA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 3)), RANK(GROWTH(RATIO(capx, at), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms generating sales growth without proportional hiring should earn higher returns when their investment profile is R&D-heavy rather than capex-growth-heavy.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: This moves away from equity-issuance use-of-proceeds and focuses on operating scalability from intangible investment. The sales-versus-headcount gate identifies potential intangible operating leverage, while the R&D-versus-capex spread separates knowledge-led scalability from physical expansion.
